finding.claim: Stored OAuth refresh_token and client_secret are sent to whichever token endpoint an authorization server selected by the MCP server's PRM names. No check binds stored credentials to the issuer that minted them, so a malicious or compromised MCP server can capture them.
finding.source: 401 response from the MCP endpoint: WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata (lib/mcp/client/http.rb:465-470, 415-421) and the origin PRM (lib/mcp/client/oauth/discovery.rb:79-90). Precondition: stored refresh_token or pre-registered client_secret, and a malicious or compromised MCP server.
finding.sink: Token-endpoint POST: refresh_token form field (lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:661-669, via refresh! at 137-187) and client_secret in the Basic Authorization header (flow.rb:681-697, 696), sent to token_endpoint from attacker-chosen AS metadata (flow.rb:700-707).

trace.note: Faraday::UnauthorizedError from MCP endpoint triggers run_oauth_flow!
run_oauth_flow! calls attempt_refresh when a refresh token is stored
attempt_refresh calls flow.refresh! with server-supplied resource_metadata_url
refresh! calls locate_authorization_server using PRM from server origin or resource_metadata
AS is authorization_servers[0] from PRM, with no check against the issuer that issued stored tokens
exchange_refresh_token posts refresh_token and client_id to attacker-chosen token_endpoint
post_to_token_endpoint adds client_secret as Basic auth to the same endpoint
Same root cause, second path: run! client_credentials branch posts client_secret (run_client_credentials! at 102-113) to attacker-chosen token endpoint when no refresh token exists

finding.guards_checked: ensure_secure_url! and ensure_secure_endpoints! (flow.rb:380-392) require HTTPS only; ensure_issuer_matches! (flow.rb:402-412) checks metadata issuer equals its own discovery URL, not the stored credential's issuer; canonical_resource/resource_covers? (flow.rb:513-525, discovery.rb:306-324) check audience of the MCP URL only; ensure_client_registered (flow.rb:414-418) reuses stored client_info without AS check; no redirects followed (default Faraday). Access token already goes to MCP server on every request (client/http.rb:367-368), so the new exposure is the long-lived refresh token and client_secret. Assumes malicious or compromised MCP server, flagged per org policy as an authentication-binding concern.
